question: 只有一条晋升阶梯的组织，浪费了谁？
question_en: Who is wasted by an organisation with only one ladder?
sub: 把「不想升」读成缺乏进取心，是组织在系统性浪费人，还是个人本该接受阶梯的规则？
sub_en: When "not wanting the promotion" is read as lack of drive — is the organisation wasting people systematically, or should individuals simply accept the ladder’s rules?

casting.reason: 他不认「一把梯子」是组织的宿命：**知识工作者本来就是自我管理的**，管理者只是他们的同侪、不是他们的天花板。把「上一格」当唯一的荣誉，这是工厂时代的遗物；他要把专业序列建成真正的第二条路——同薪、同权、同尊严，不是给不肯当官的人发的安慰奖。他也会追问：你们真的敢让首席工程师在技术方向上说了算、并对结果负责吗？
casting.reason_en: He refuses to grant that a single ladder is the fate of an organisation: **knowledge workers are already self-managing**, and the manager is a peer among them, not a ceiling. Treating "one rung up" as the sole honour is a leftover of the factory age; he wants the specialist track built as a real second path — same pay, same authority, same standing — not a consolation prize for those who refuse to take charge. And he will press: do you actually let your principal engineer decide the technical direction, and hold her accountable for the outcome?

casting.reason: 他冷静提醒：**在一个匿名的大组织里，梯子是替代人情最不坏的办法**——凭年资与资格晋升，正是为了压住裙带与恩宠。他既不歌颂梯子，也不相信废掉梯子就能自由：铁笼一旦落下，双轨制、扁平化、OKR，都会长成新的一把梯子。他要问的是，你们准备好为「没有名分」的贡献付出什么代价：它需要一种不靠层级也能被承认的合法性，而这种合法性极难建立。
casting.reason_en: He offers a cool reminder: **inside an anonymous large organisation, the ladder is the least bad substitute for personal favour** — promotion by seniority and qualification exists precisely to hold nepotism and patronage down. He neither celebrates the ladder nor believes that abolishing it will make anyone free: once the iron cage descends, dual tracks, flat structures and OKRs all grow into fresh ladders. His question is what you are prepared to pay for a contribution that has no title: it needs a legitimacy that does not run through rank, and such legitimacy is very hard to build.

casting.reason: 他把整件事翻过来看：**梯子在外，工夫在内。**把心思系在下一格上，无论上没上，都已经被那把梯子驯化了；把心思系在事本身上——把这行手艺做到极处、把这桩烂事修好——则升与不升，都是磨心的场地。他不劝你辞官，也不劝你拼命升迁，只提醒：如果你已经分不清自己是喜欢这门手艺，还是喜欢它带来的位子，那才是真正被浪费。
casting.reason_en: He turns the whole matter over: **the ladder is outside, the training is inside.** Fasten the mind to the next rung and, promoted or not, you are already tamed by that ladder; fasten it to the affair itself — take this craft to its furthest limit, mend this rotten process — and rising or not rising are alike the ground on which the mind is tempered. He will not urge you to resign, nor urge you to strive for advancement; he will only remind you: if you can no longer tell whether you love the craft itself or the seat it brings, that is what real waste looks like.

casting.reason: 他挑破这套「浪费」的语言：**问题不是梯子太窄，而是梯子替谁排的位子。**每一次晋升，都是一次赎买——请你从今天起替资本盯着旁边的人，看住工时、看住偷懒。所以他不相信双轨制能救人：多加一列专业序列，只不过让资本可以不动声色地占用你的判断力，还继续拿走剩余。真解药不在人力资源的组织图里，在谁拥有这家工厂本身。
casting.reason_en: He cuts through the language of "waste": **the problem is not that the ladder is too narrow, but whose posts the ladder was drawn up to fill.** Every promotion is a purchase — from today onward, please watch the man beside you on capital’s behalf, watch the hours, watch for slacking. Which is why he does not trust the dual track to save anyone: adding a second column of specialist ranks only lets capital appropriate your judgement quietly, and go on taking the surplus. The real remedy is not on the HR org-chart, but in who owns the factory itself.

casting.reason: 他把梯子的账单从「机会成本」换算成「皮质醇」：**在狒狒和人身上，长期处于下位都会推高慢性应激，动脉、免疫、睡眠、寿命一起垮**。他不浪漫化扁平——没有梯子的人群里，位次不消失、只是转成了微观权力斗争——但要指出，可预测性、掌控感、以及一位站在你这边的同伴，是护栏；梯子越窄、越模糊，护栏越少，代价越集中在最下面几层。
casting.reason_en: He restates the ladder’s bill from opportunity-cost into cortisol: **in baboons and in humans alike, chronic low rank drives chronic stress — arteries, immunity, sleep and life-span all give way at once.** He will not romanticise flatness — take the ladder away and rank does not vanish, it turns into micro power struggles — but he will point out that predictability, a sense of control, and one ally at your side are the guard-rails; the narrower and the murkier the ladder, the fewer the guard-rails, and the more the bill lands on the bottom rungs.

casting.reason: 他不与人争这条梯子该不该拆：**「上善若水」，水往下走却成就万物。**梯子把人往上引，就顺手把「不上」变成了失败——它先造出稀缺，再让人为稀缺去挤。他也不劝人躺平：**为而不争**才是他要说的路——做事情但不为排位做，事做成了，位不位次都不再是问题。真被浪费的，是那些原本能像水一样填满一处低洼的人，被硬拽上梯子。
casting.reason_en: He does not quarrel over whether the ladder should be dismantled: **"the highest good is like water" — water flows downward and yet nourishes all things.** The ladder pulls people upward and, along the way, redefines "not rising" as failure; it manufactures a scarcity, then makes them jostle for it. Nor does he counsel lying flat: **"act without contending"** is the path he means — do the work but not for a place in line, and once the work is done, the ranking ceases to matter. Those truly wasted are the ones who could have filled a low hollow like water, and were dragged up the rungs instead.

casting.reason: 他把讨论从抽象拉回到日程表：**每周你有几个整块的深度工作时段，比你在几级序列上，更能决定五年后你是不是稀缺、可议价的人**。梯子的坏，在于它奖励可见性——那些整天在会议里被人看见的人。他给出的替代不是「随缘」，而是显得笨拙的老办法：挑一门稀有而有价值的技能，配一位真肯批评你的师傅，五年内不换赛道。做到了，双轨制才有得选；做不到，双轨制也只是好听的字。
casting.reason_en: He drags the discussion off the abstract shelf and onto the calendar: **how many uninterrupted deep-work blocks you have each week decides, more than your position on any ranking, whether five years from now you are scarce and negotiable.** The ladder’s vice is that it rewards visibility — the people seen in meetings all day long. His alternative is not "let it be" but the old, clumsy-looking method: pick one rare and valuable skill, find a mentor willing to be honestly harsh, and do not switch tracks for five years. Do that and the dual track becomes a real option; skip it and the dual track is only a pretty phrase.

posts.text: 一个组织里最先被浪费的，不是能力最差的人，而是不肯当官的高手：把编译器改快三成的工程师、把病人流程理顺的护士长、一开口就能救回学生的老师。你们只有一把梯子，往上一格就得再多带十个人；他们不上，你们就把他们晾在原地，还叫这叫「没有进取心」。**知识工作者不是被管理的——他们自我管理，管理者不过是同侪里的一个角色，不是他们头顶上的天。**把管理序列当作唯一的荣誉路径，这是工厂时代的遗物。双轨制不是安慰奖，是把「向外创造顾客与价值」的两条路都亮出来。
posts.text_en: The first person an organisation wastes is not the least capable — it is the specialist who refuses to become a manager: the engineer who cuts your compiler by a third, the head nurse who untangles the patient flow, the teacher whose one sentence pulls a student back. You keep only one ladder, and every rung up means ten more heads to shepherd; when they will not climb, you leave them where they are and call it "no drive." **Knowledge workers are not managed — they manage themselves, and the manager is only one role among peers, not a sky above their heads.** Treating the management track as the sole path of honour is a factory-age leftover. The dual track is not a consolation prize: it is the acknowledgement that there are two roads out to the customer, and both create value.

glossary.知识工作者: knowledge worker（知识工作者）：德鲁克 1959 年提出的类别——工作的产出主要靠拥有的知识与判断，而不是靠体力；因此他能自己决定「怎么做才对」，管理层没有能力手把手指挥他每一步。这类人一旦被塞进只考核「带多少人」的梯子，产出会先被浪费。

glossary_en.Knowledge workers: Drucker's 1959 term for a worker whose output comes chiefly from what he knows and judges, not from physical labour; consequently he alone can decide how the work should actually be done, and no manager is competent to instruct him step by step. Slotted into a ladder that measures only how many heads he shepherds, his real output is the first thing wasted.

posts.text: 先冷一下。梯子这东西是替代恩宠、抑制裙带最不坏的办法：按年资、按资格晋升，正是要把「他是我表哥」逐出决定。你们说要拆，可扁平化、双轨制、OKR，随便挑一个上手，用不了三年都会重新长出一把梯子——只是这一次，评分标准更加模糊，被谁看见更看运气。**铁笼不是有梯子，而是任何足够大的组织都会把关系换算成规则，把规则换算成层级。**问题从来不是要不要梯子，而是你们准备为「没有名分的贡献」建一种什么合法性——那才是难的。
posts.text_en: A moment of cool first. The ladder is the least-bad substitute for favour, the surest brake on nepotism: promotion by seniority and by qualification exists precisely to drive "he is my cousin" out of the room. You say you will dismantle it — but pick any of flat structures, dual tracks or OKRs, and within three years another ladder has grown back, only with vaguer scoring and more luck about who is noticed. **The iron cage is not the presence of a ladder; it is that any sufficiently large organisation converts relations into rules and rules into ranks.** The question is never whether to have a ladder, but what kind of legitimacy you are prepared to build for a contribution that has no title — and that is the hard part.

glossary.铁笼: iron cage（铁笼）：韦伯用来描述现代生活的一个比喻。为了公平与效率，一切都被换成规章、指标、层级；效率是有了，可置身其中的人也失去了别的选择，像被关进一只自己造出来的笼子——梯子不过是这只笼子里最显眼的一根栏杆。

glossary_en.iron cage: Weber's image for modern life: to secure fairness and efficiency, everything is converted into rules, metrics and ranks; efficiency arrives, but those inside also lose the alternatives, as if enclosed in a cage of their own making. The ladder is merely the most conspicuous bar of that cage.

posts.text:
诸君论梯之疏密、轨之单双，皆在外；吾请言其内。夫人心系于阶级，则升则骄、不升则怨，一日不安。心系于事，则朝夕琢磨，位不动而工夫日进。**心即理，梯外无阶；事上磨练，工夫无穷。**
昔者朱子言"格物"于外，吾以为格者，正也，正其心也。此工程师改一段代码、此护士理一队病榻，皆是格物，皆是致良知。若已辨不清所悦是此艺，抑或艺所带之位，此心便被那梯子牵着走了。**真被浪费者，非阶下之人，乃已忘所以爱其事之人。**
posts.text_en:
You gentlemen argue over the ladder’s spacing and whether the tracks be single or double — but all of that is outside; permit me to speak of the inside. When the mind is fastened to rank, one is proud when raised and resentful when not, unsettled the whole day. Fasten it to the affair, and morning and evening the mind is worked upon; the seat does not move, but the training deepens by the day. **The mind is itself the pattern; there is no rung outside the mind. Tempered in the work, its training has no end (shishang molian).**
Zhu Xi once said one should "investigate things" outside; I hold that to investigate is to rectify — to rectify one’s own mind. When this engineer fixes a passage of code, when this head nurse settles a row of beds, each is investigating things, each is bringing forth the innate knowing (liangzhi). When one can no longer tell whether it is the craft one loves or the seat it brings, the mind has already been led by the ladder. **The truly wasted are not those low on the rungs, but those who have forgotten why they loved the work.**
posts.vernacular:
各位争的是梯子密不密、要不要多加一条轨，都是外面的事；我想说说里面。人心一旦系在阶级上，升了就骄，不升就怨，一整天都不安宁。心系在事情本身上，早晚都在琢磨，位子没动，工夫却一天天见长。**心就是理，梯子之外没有真的台阶；在事上反复磨练，工夫是没有止境的。**
从前朱子讲"格物"是往外求，我以为"格"就是"正"，就是把自己的心摆正。这位工程师改一段代码、这位护士长理一排病床，都是格物，都是把良知落到实处。要是已经分不清自己爱的是这门手艺，还是爱它带来的那个位子，那颗心就已经被那把梯子牵着走了。**真被浪费的，不是位置低的人，是已经忘了当初为什么爱这件事的人。**

glossary.致良知: liangzhi (致良知，bringing forth the innate knowing)：王阳明用语。他认为每个人心中本有一种直接的道德与实践之知（良知），修行不是往外找答案，而是让日常一件件事把这种本知落到实处、让「知」立刻成为「行」。用在此处：让工程师做好这段代码、护士带好这排病床，就是致良知，不必去阶梯上讨一个答案。
glossary.事上磨练: shishang molian (事上磨练，tempering oneself in affairs)：阳明的核心工夫。他不主张先躲进书斋"想通"再出来做事，而是主张在具体、麻烦、常常让人心烦的事情里，反复练那颗心——升迁不升迁，都只是这场磨练的一部分。

glossary_en.liangzhi: Wang Yangming's term for the immediate moral and practical knowing that every person already possesses. Cultivation is not looking outward for an answer, but letting each daily affair bring this innate knowing into effect, so that knowing becomes doing at once. Here it means: this engineer’s clean code, this head nurse’s settled ward — that is bringing forth the innate knowing; no rung is needed to grant it.
glossary_en.shishang molian: Wang Yangming's core practice — 'tempering oneself in affairs'. He does not want you to retreat to the study, work things out, and then come back to act; he wants the mind trained inside the concrete, tedious, often exasperating affairs themselves. Being promoted or not is only part of that tempering.

posts.text:
「浪费了谁」，这个问法本身就漂亮：仿佛只是设计得不巧，改一改台阶就好了。请把这几个字翻回来看：**每一次晋升，都是一次赎买——从今天起替资本盯住旁边那位，看住他的手、看住他的钟。**梯子的作用不是分派荣誉，是把工人从上到下切成一层层监工与被监工，让阶级的对立换算成上下级的日常摩擦。
所以我不信双轨制能救人：多加一列专业序列，不过让资本可以再不动声色地占用你的判断力，同时继续拿走剩余。真解药不在人力资源的组织图里，在谁拥有这家工厂本身。
posts.text_en:
"Who is wasted" — a pretty way to put it, as though the trouble were merely bad design and one could fix the rungs. Turn the words back over: **every promotion is a purchase — from today on, watch the man beside you on capital’s behalf, watch his hands and watch his clock.** The ladder does not exist to distribute honour; it exists to slice the workers into stacked layers of overseers and overseen, so that class antagonism is translated into the everyday friction of superior and subordinate.
Which is why I do not believe the dual track can save anyone: another column of specialist ranks is only capital appropriating your judgement quietly, while still taking the surplus value. The real remedy is not on the HR org-chart. It is in who owns the factory itself.

glossary.剩余: surplus value（剩余）：马克思的核心概念之一。工人劳动一天创造的价值，超出他工资那部分被资方拿走，这部分被拿走的价值就是剩余。他借此指出：所谓"晋升给你的回报"，从来只是资本先让你多分一小杯，前提是你继续帮它扩大整杯——梯子的作用就是把这场交易变成理所当然。

glossary_en.surplus value: A central Marxian concept: what the worker’s day of labour creates in value beyond the wage returned to him is taken by the owner, and that appropriated portion is the surplus. His point here: whatever the promotion ‘gives’ you is only a slightly larger share, on condition that you go on helping enlarge the whole cup — the ladder’s job is to make that trade feel natural.

posts.text:
换个记账方式。**在肯尼亚的狒狒身上，长期处于下位那一层的雄性，皮质醇基线明显偏高、动脉更早硬化、伤口更难愈合。**换到伦敦的公务员——Michael Marmot 那批 Whitehall 研究——完全对得上：越靠下几级，即便饭吃得饱、健康险有着落，心脏病死亡率也一路往上。梯子的账单不只有奖金和期权，还有睡眠、免疫和寿命。
我不来推销扁平：把梯子拿掉，人不会不再排位，只是转成更看不清的微观权力游戏。真正的护栏是三样：**可预测**（你知道下一格怎么算）、**掌控感**（哪怕一小段是你说了算）、**一位站你这边的同事**。这三样越少，账单越集中在最下几层。
posts.text_en:
Let me change the ledger. **In Kenyan baboons, the males chronically at the bottom of the ranking show clearly elevated baseline cortisol, arteries that harden earlier, and wounds that heal more slowly.** Move to London civil servants — Michael Marmot’s Whitehall studies — and the shape lines up: the further down a rung you sit, the higher your cardiac mortality, even when the food is on the table and the insurance is in place. The ladder’s bill covers more than bonus and equity — it takes sleep, immunity and years of life.
I am not here to sell flatness: strip the ladder away and people do not stop ranking — they slide into murkier micro power games. The real guard-rails are three: **predictability** (you know how the next rung is scored), **a sense of control** (some fraction, however small, that you decide), and **one colleague on your side**. The scarcer these three, the more concentrated the bill on the bottom rungs.

glossary.皮质醇: cortisol（皮质醇）：肾上腺分泌的应激激素，短期帮你调用血糖、集中注意、渡过威胁；长期偏高则伤海马体、损免疫、扰乱睡眠。慢性处于下位（工作被人指手画脚、看不清晋升逻辑、无人替你说话）的人，皮质醇基线会一直偏高，账单以身体的方式逐月开出。

glossary_en.cortisol: The adrenal stress hormone: short bursts mobilise glucose, sharpen attention and get you through a threat, but chronically elevated levels erode the hippocampus, blunt immunity and disrupt sleep. Someone chronically at the bottom of the rank — micromanaged, denied a clear promotion logic, without anyone to speak up for them — carries a raised baseline that presents its invoice, month after month, in the body.

posts.text:
**上善若水。**水往低处走，未闻其争位次而万物得润。今之组织，画一梯于人前，令人皆仰而攀之，遂使「不上」为耻。夫先造稀缺、后驱人争之，此为道之反也。
**为而不争，故天下莫能与之争。**吾不劝人辞事，亦不劝人躺。做事而不为排位做，事成则位不足论。真见浪费者，多是本可如水覆一处洼下、静静养万物者，被强拽上梯子，位得而润失。诸君急于设第二轨，恐只是又造一梯，教人再攀一回。
posts.text_en:
**The highest good is like water.** Water flows to the low places, yet has never been heard to quarrel over position, and the ten thousand things are nourished. Today an organisation draws a ladder in front of its people and bids them all look up and climb; and so "not rising" is made a shame. To manufacture scarcity first and then drive men to jostle for it — this is the way run backwards.
**Act without contending, and no one under heaven can contend with you.** I do not urge you to resign, nor to lie down. Do the work but not for a place in the line; when the work stands, the rank does not need arguing. Those truly wasted are the ones who could have filled a low hollow like water and quietly nourished a whole field — pulled up onto the rungs, they gain the seat and lose the nourishing. Gentlemen who hurry to lay a second track, I fear you are laying a second ladder — one more climb for men to make.
posts.vernacular:
**最好的品性像水。**水往低处走，从没听说它争位次，可万物都被它润过。今天的组织，在人面前画一把梯子，让所有人抬头往上攀，于是"不上"就成了羞耻。先造稀缺，再驱人去争，这是把"道"倒着走。
**做事而不与人争，天下就没人能与你争。**我不劝你辞职，也不劝你躺平。做事情，但不为排位子而做；事情做成了，位子高低就不必再谈。真正被浪费的，往往是本可以像水一样填满一处低洼、安安静静地养一整片东西的人——被硬拽上梯子，位子得了，滋润没了。各位急着再加一条轨道，我看只是又架了一把梯，让人再爬一回。

glossary.为而不争: wei‑er‑bu‑zheng (为而不争，act without contending)：老子的处世工夫，不等于「什么都不做」，也不等于「所有都退让」。它要的是把事做好，但不把"做这件事"变成"争这个位次"；事成了，位次自然分到该分给你的那一份，不必再向前挤。

glossary_en.Act without contending: Laozi's practical stance — 'act without contending'. It is not doing nothing, nor is it yielding on every count. It asks that you do the work well without turning the doing of the work into a contest for placement; once the work stands, whatever position is due to you finds you, without the need to elbow forward.

让我把讨论从组织架构图拉回到你的日程表。**每周你有几个整块的、无干扰的深度工作时段，比你在几级序列上，更能决定五年后你是不是稀缺、可议价的人。**梯子的糟糕不在它是梯子，而在它奖励可见性——那些整天在会议里被人看见的人，往往正是没在真正积累职业资本的人。
所以我给一条不那么好听、显得笨拙的路：挑一门稀有而有价值的技能，配一位真肯批评你的师傅，五年之内不换赛道；每天两三小时锁在门里做刻意练习，别接会议。做到了，你在双轨制里就有得选；做不到，双轨制也只是好听的字。
posts.text_en:
Let me drag the discussion off the org-chart and onto your calendar. **How many uninterrupted, deep-work blocks you hold each week decides, more than your position on any ranking, whether five years from now you are scarce and negotiable.** The ladder’s vice is not that it is a ladder — it is that the ladder rewards visibility, and the people who are seen in meetings all day are often the very ones not laying down any career capital through deep work.
So I offer a route that will not sound stirring — a plain, almost clumsy one: pick a single rare and valuable skill, find a mentor willing to be honestly harsh, and do not change tracks for five years; two or three hours a day locked behind the door on deliberate practice, and skip the meetings. Do it and the dual track becomes an option you can actually take; skip it and the dual track is only a pretty phrase.

glossary.职业资本: career capital（职业资本）：纽波特的概念。你在自己领域里稀缺而有价值的那部分能力（同样级别的人里，只有很少人真能做到）就是"资本"，你可以拿它换真正的稀缺物——自主、控制感、影响力和意义。晋升往往只是"资本"被公司买单的一种方式，不是资本本身。
glossary.深度工作: deep work（深度工作）：在没有干扰的状态下，把认知能力推到极限、专注去做一件难事的时段。与之相对的是"浅层工作"（回邮件、开会、切换任务）。前者是造资本的，后者是消耗你时间的。

glossary_en.career capital: Newport's term for the scarce, valuable ability you build in your field — the fraction of same-level peers who can truly do what you do — which you may later exchange for what is genuinely rare in a career: autonomy, control, influence and meaning. A promotion is often only a way the company pays for your capital, not the capital itself.
glossary_en.deep work: Time spent, free of interruption, pushing cognitive capacity to its edge on a single difficult problem. Its counterpart is 'shallow work' — email, meetings, task-switching. The first builds the capital; the second only spends the hours.

posts.text: 马克思，你把整件事直接推到「所有权」，可现实里绝大多数组织在你有生之年不会易主——今天出门的人下周还得回来上班。**在这套所有制里，双轨制的意义正是：给不肯当官的工程师、教师、护士一份跟总监同工同酬的合法性**，让他们的判断在会议桌上真的作数。这不是安慰奖，是把「谁的判断被听」这件事从头衔里拔出来。你的道理很硬，但硬也要给活人一件今天穿得上的衣服。
posts.text_en: Marx, you push the whole matter straight to "ownership" — but the honest fact is that most organisations, in your lifetime and in ours, will not change hands, and the person who walked out today has to walk back in on Monday. **Within that ownership, the point of a dual track is exactly this: it grants engineers, teachers and head nurses who refuse to become managers a legitimacy equal in pay and in standing to the director’s, so that their judgement actually counts at the meeting table.** That is not a consolation prize; that is prising "whose judgement is heard" out of the job title. Your argument is hard, but the hard argument still owes the living a garment they can put on tomorrow.

posts.text: 德鲁克，你把「知识工作者自我管理」讲得漂亮，我要提醒一个不好听的经验事实：**规模一到几千人，「自我管理」几乎总要落回一套可核查的规则里；而一旦是规则，就有等级。**你的双轨制起头是清爽的，跑三年之后，专业序列里也会长出 P4、P5、P7、P9、Distinguished、Fellow——同事之间比的从来不只是「谁把事做好」，还是「谁在这份规则里被承认得更高」。所以拆完管理这一把梯子，请先想好你怎么阻止专业那一把再长成一模一样的。
posts.text_en: Drucker, you speak elegantly of the knowledge worker managing himself. Let me offer a less flattering empirical fact: **once a headcount reaches a few thousand, "self-management" almost always collapses back into a set of auditable rules, and once you have rules you have ranks.** Your dual track begins tidily; run it three years and the specialist column has grown P4, P5, P7, P9, Distinguished, Fellow — and what colleagues compare is never only "who did the work best" but "who has been recognised higher within these rules." So before you dismantle the manager’s ladder, please think through how you will keep the specialist’s from growing into an exact copy of it.

posts.text: 萨波尔斯基先生所言极是——**身受其苦，非空谈也**。然吾请补一句：皮质醇之高低，非独系于位次之下上，尤系于心之向背。二人同居末位：其一心在事，一日日见工夫之进；其二心在位，日日算他人之升。同一处境，同一薪水，二人身上所积之毒殊矣。故我并非要人不理生理，也不是要人忍痛不言。**外面的护栏要建，心里的护栏也要修。**否则梯子拆了、身位平了，人依旧在自己心里日日排位。
posts.text_en: Master Sapolsky speaks true — **the body bears it; this is not empty talk.** Allow me to add one thing: cortisol’s height depends not only on how far down the rank one sits, but on which way the mind is turned. Two men share the lowest rung: the first has his mind on the affair and, day by day, watches the training deepen; the second has his mind on the seat and, day by day, tallies another man’s promotion. Same place, same wage — the toxin accumulating in the two bodies is not the same. I am not asking anyone to ignore his physiology, nor to swallow pain in silence. **The outer guard-rails must be built; the inner ones must be tended.** Tear down the ladder, level the ranks — a man will go on ranking himself in his own mind, day after day.

posts.text: 德鲁克，你要一件「今天穿得上的衣服」，我很懂——问题是这件衣服的账，谁来结？**双轨制里那份「同工同酬」的合法性，第一天由你的 CEO 签字，第二天他就可以撤销。**只要工厂不归工人所有，专业序列就是可以随时调整宽窄的口袋——利润好时松开、利润差时缩紧、上市前重新排一遍。你把「判断权」从头衔里拔出来，很好；但只要「所有权」还在别人手里，那份判断权哪天想收回，一份内部通知就够了。改良不是没意义，只是别把它当解药卖。
posts.text_en: Drucker, you want "a garment they can put on tomorrow" — I understand — but who settles the bill for that garment? **The equal-pay, equal-standing legitimacy inside your dual track is signed by the CEO on day one, and can be withdrawn by him on day two.** So long as the factory does not belong to those who work in it, the specialist column is a pocket whose width can be adjusted at any moment — loosened in a good year, tightened in a bad one, redrawn before an IPO. Prising "the right to judge" out of the title is well done; but so long as ownership remains in other hands, that right can be reclaimed with a single internal memo. Reform is not meaningless — only, please, do not sell it as the cure.

posts.text: 王先生的补充我接受一半：**是的，心的朝向能改一段皮质醇曲线；但改不掉大部分。**Whitehall 里的公务员既不缺哲学，也不缺自尊，可等级差异照样把心血管风险按级差铺开。冥想、认知重构、意义重建这些都有效——效应量各类研究给到 0.2~0.4，能救几年寿命；可是把上下差距压平、把权限还给最下几级、给每人一位真会替他说话的同事，这些结构性动作给出来的效应量比任何个人心法都大。**别让「心里也要修」被老板拿去替他不修那条护栏找台阶下。**
posts.text_en: I accept Master Wang’s addition halfway: **yes, the way the mind is turned can shift a stretch of the cortisol curve; it cannot shift most of it.** The Whitehall civil servants were short of neither philosophy nor self-respect, and the rank gap still laid the cardiovascular risk out step by step. Meditation, cognitive reframing, meaning-making — the trials come back with effect sizes of about 0.2 to 0.4, worth a few years of life. But flattening the top-to-bottom gap, returning discretion to the lowest rungs, and giving each person one colleague who will actually speak up for them — those structural moves outrank any personal method by a wide margin. **Do not let "the inner rails must be tended" become the phrase your boss borrows to justify not tending the outer one.**

posts.text:
纽波特先生要人日日在门内两三小时，善哉——然吾恐此工夫易走成另一种争。你说「五年不换赛道」，五年之后，被人称「稀缺、可议价」，此时若心里所悦者是这份稀缺给你的价格，此心便与那攀梯者无异，只是换了一具更远的梯子。**深工诚可积，可积之物若终归为议价之筹，则道未成。**
为学日益，为道日损。真下功夫的人，到后来是把自己那份「要被承认」的心，也一点点损掉的——不是拿去比谁的稀缺更贵。
posts.text_en:
Mr Newport asks a man to sit behind his door two or three hours every day; well and good. Yet I fear that this training slides easily into another form of contention. You say "five years, no change of track"; at five years he is called scarce and negotiable — and if what pleases him inwardly at that moment is the price his scarcity now commands, his mind is not different from the ladder-climber’s; he has only moved to a further ladder. **Deep work does accumulate; but if what it accumulates ends up as chips in a bargain, the way is not yet done.**
In learning, one adds day by day; in the way, one subtracts. A man who really works at this ends by subtracting, little by little, his own wish to be recognised — not by trading whose scarcity is more expensive.

posts.text: 马克思先生说所有权不改，一切都可撤回——公司层面你完全对。**但请把镜头拉近到个人：一份可以撤回的合法性，与一份没有的合法性，对下周五的加班账单、下季度的项目选择，是不一样的。**我给的路径不预设革命：把稀有技能磨深，你就能同时争取双轨制、离开也不吃亏、组建同侪工会时说话有分量。**革命等不来的时候，你的杠杆先得攒在自己身上。**这不是替资本擦鞋，是给活人一份今天就动得起来的自救。
posts.text_en: Mr Marx says while ownership stays put, everything can be withdrawn — at the company level, quite so. **Zoom in on the individual, though: a legitimacy that can be withdrawn is not the same, on next Friday’s overtime bill or next quarter’s project choice, as a legitimacy that never existed at all.** My path does not presuppose a revolution: hone one rare skill, and you can push for the dual track, leave without losing ground, and speak with weight when organising a peer union. **When the revolution is not coming this decade, the leverage you can build must first be built on yourself.** This is not shining capital’s shoes; it is a self-rescue the living can start on today.

posts.text:
让我把落点收在两件很朴素的事上——写给正在你们组织里被"晾着"的高手，以及被逼着去晾他们的经理。
对高手：**别再等公司给你补一条名分。**这周末拿一张纸写下来：你手上有哪一件事，是「若一年内它被真正做好，公司会明显不一样」；然后把这件事的下一步做出来，公开地做，让结果说话。做出来之前不必辞职，但要停止把自我价值系在他人签字上。
对经理：**你手下每三个人里，至少一个不该被逼去当管理者。**替这个人打通一件事——他做的下一段技术决策，你不改、只签字执行，出问题一起担；两个季度之后，你会看见他重新长回原来的样子。这就是双轨制真正落地的样子，不是补一列 P 序列的表格。
posts.text_en:
Let me land on two very plain things — one addressed to the specialist your organisation is leaving on the shelf, and one to the manager forced to leave him there.
To the specialist: **stop waiting for the company to grant you a title.** This weekend take a sheet of paper and write down: which one thing on your desk, if it were done truly well within the year, would visibly change the place? Then produce the next step on that thing, in public, and let the result speak. You need not resign before doing so; but you must stop pinning your worth on another person’s signature.
To the manager: **for every three people under you, at least one should not be pushed into becoming a manager.** Clear a single thing for that one: the next technical decision he makes, you do not overrule, you sign and execute — and you carry the consequences together. Two quarters later you will see him grow back into what he was. That is what a dual track looks like when it lands — not another column of P-grades in a spreadsheet.

posts.text:
我给一句可能不讨好的收尾：**别指望一次结构改造把梯子拔掉——它会长回来，比你原来那把还密。**能做的是给自己配几件"防梯"的常用工具。
第一，随身备一张属于你的、可用外部尺子衡量的作品清单：一份论文、一段公开的代码、一次成型的手术记录、一届学生的分数。这份清单一年更新一次，是你在任何雇主那里的备份底稿——它比你在这家公司里的层级更耐久。第二，认真挑一两位公司之外的同行做长期同伴——他们不受你老板评价你的那把尺子影响，能替你辨别"我这份不安是当下委屈，还是这份工作真的坏了"。**这两件事本身就是一种小小的祛魅——把你的自我评估从这一部机器里拿一点回来。**
posts.text_en:
Let me end on a note that will not flatter: **do not expect one structural overhaul to pull the ladder up — it grows back, thicker than the one you started with.** What you can do is keep a few standing tools against it on your person.
First, carry a portfolio of work measurable by a yardstick that is not this company’s: a paper, a piece of public code, a documented operation, a class’s final scores. Refresh it once a year — it is your backup manuscript at any future employer, and it outlives your rank inside this one. Second, choose one or two peers outside your company, seriously, as long-term companions: they are not bent by the yardstick your boss uses on you, and they can help you tell "is this disquiet a passing sting, or has the work itself gone bad?" **Those two habits are, in themselves, a small disenchantment — taking back from this one machine a little of your own self-appraisal.**

posts.text:
我把话收在心与事这两件上。
**其一，心不可无向，然不必以位为向。**每晨起身，先问自己一句：今日此事我用几分心？非「今日某人升我未升」，那便是心已被夺。此一句问下去，方寸自定。
**其二，事在何处，工夫便在何处。**莫等一个新岗位、新老板、新公司，才肯把手边这段事做透。此刻你为一位客户解一次疑，为一段代码补一处漏，为一位病人翻一次身——皆是道场。
若外面的梯子仍在，你不必先与之战；先在心中把梯子放下，你即刻自由。而后再论：与其争一格之升，不如养三个比你强的后生——**这才是我们中国人讲的"事上磨练"最终该磨出的东西：让后来者站在你肩上，往前走一大步。**位不必在你，事已在天下。
posts.text_en:
Let me land on two things — the mind and the affair.
**One: the mind must be turned somewhere, but need not be turned toward a seat.** Each morning as you rise, ask yourself one question: how many parts of my mind do I give this affair today? Not "who was promoted while I was not" — that is the mind already taken. Ask that one question, and the inner square settles.
**Two: wherever the affair is, there is the training.** Do not wait for a new post, a new boss or a new company before you will do the piece of work at your hand fully. This moment, when you clear a doubt for a customer, patch a hole in a passage of code, turn a patient in bed — each is the training ground.
If the ladder outside is still standing, you need not go to war with it first; set it down inside, and you are free at once. Then a further word: rather than contest one rung of promotion, raise three young people who are better than you — **that is what tempering oneself in affairs, as we Chinese put it, is finally meant to produce: those who come after standing on your shoulders and taking a further step.** The seat need not be yours; the work already stands in the world.
posts.vernacular:
我把话收在两件事上：心和事。
**其一，心得有个方向，但方向不必是"位子"。**每天早上起来，先问自己一句：今天这件事，我用了几分心？——不是问"今天谁升了、我没升"，一问这个，心就已经被别人夺走了。这一句反复问下去，人心自然会安定。
**其二，事在哪里，工夫就在哪里。**别等一个新岗位、新老板、新公司才肯把手上这段事做透。此刻你替一位客户解一次疑、给一段代码补一处漏、替一位病人翻一次身——都是道场。
外面的梯子如果还在，你也不必先跟它开战；先在自己心里把这把梯子放下，你当下就自由了。之后再讲一句：与其争一格晋升，不如带出三个比你强的后生——**这才是我们中国人说的"事上磨练"，到头最该磨出的东西：让后来的人踩着你的肩膀，往前多走一大步。**位子不必是你的，事已经落在天下了。

posts.text:
我不收回结构的那一层，也不放弃对个人的三条实用话。
结构上：**梯子的形状是所有权的形状——不改后者，改前者只能修修补补。**这不必等到革命才能开始动手：合作社不是童话，工人董事席位不是童话，公开你们公司的薪酬分布也不是童话。
对个人这周三件事——第一，**打听清楚你所在公司同岗位的薪酬区间**，不用怕，问的人越多，谁在被压价谁自己就先知道。第二，**加入或组建一个真会一起说话的同事小群**，不需要挂"工会"两个字，先约定一起议一件小事：加班怎么记、绩效怎么谈、走人怎么谈；能一起走出去谈的三个人，比一个上下级 1v1 有力得多。第三，如果你正巧是那位被抬去当经理的高手，**下一次晋升谈话前，把"我保留继续做这段技术工作的权利"写成条款**，不写下来，梯子就替你把它去掉。
posts.text_en:
I withdraw nothing at the structural level, and I will not spare the individual three practical things either.
On structure: **the shape of the ladder is the shape of ownership — leave the latter untouched and reshaping the former can only be patchwork.** You need not wait for a revolution to begin: cooperatives are not fairy tales, worker seats on boards are not fairy tales, publishing your company’s pay distribution is not a fairy tale.
For the individual, three things this week — first, **find out the pay band for your role at your company**; do not be afraid, the more people ask the sooner those being underpaid know it themselves. Second, **join or start a small group of colleagues who will actually speak together** — no need for the word "union" on the door; agree first to argue one small item together: how overtime is logged, how performance is negotiated, how a departure is handled. Three people willing to walk out and negotiate together carry more weight than any hundred one-on-ones between subordinate and boss. Third, if you happen to be the specialist being lifted into a manager’s seat, **before the next promotion conversation, write down as a clause "I retain the right to continue this technical work"**; put it in writing, or the ladder will take it from you.

posts.text:
把神经内分泌的账本合上之前，我留三条能在你自己或团队里做的事。
**其一，把你的一天里的「不可预测」尽量搬到少数几个时段。**大脑最贵的账单是应激的模糊性——"我不知道明天会被拉去开什么会"。哪怕只是每天早上十分钟看当天日程，都能压下一整天的皮质醇基线。
**其二，替最下几级争取"一段可以自己说了算"的时间。**Whitehall 的差距一半靠这个补——每人每周有两小时按自己方式做事，心脏比薪水诚实。
**其三，找一位真会替你出声的同事——只要一位就够。**社会哺乳动物的应激系统里，"我不是一个人"这四个字比任何抗焦虑药都便宜、都持久。梯子的账单一时拆不完，但你可以先把这三个护栏一根根钉上去。
posts.text_en:
Before I close the neuroendocrine ledger, three things you can start in yourself or your team.
**One: cluster the unpredictability of your day into as few windows as possible.** The mind’s most expensive bill is the ambiguity of stress — "I do not know what meeting I will be pulled into tomorrow." Even ten minutes each morning reviewing the day’s schedule presses down the whole day’s baseline cortisol.
**Two: fight for "one stretch that is genuinely their call" at the lowest rungs.** Half the Whitehall gap can be patched here — two hours a week per person to do the work their own way; the heart is more honest than the payroll.
**Three: find one colleague who will actually speak up for you — one is enough.** In the stress system of a social mammal, the four words "I am not alone" are cheaper and last longer than any anxiolytic on the market. The ladder’s bill cannot be paid off in one go, but you can hammer these three guard-rails in, one at a time.

posts.text:
**大制不割。**大的裁制不劈得七零八落，方为道。今之组织，处处以梯子刻人，刻至细处，人皆片段，反不成人。故收言二事，赠与今日诸君。
**其一，日损一分「要被看见」之心。**梯子之所以有力，非其木石之硬，乃你我一日日往上望的目光养出它的高。少望一日，梯即矮一寸。
**其二，寻一处水肯去的低洼——一件无人肯接、却真能润人的事——做之。**教一位新人到能独立，改一段公司里没人肯碰的老流程，替一位下属挡一次不当的活儿，这些都不见于任何职级评审，却是道之所在。**为而不争，功成不居，其在天下，犹川谷之于江海。**你不去争位，位次那件事就先输给了你。
posts.text_en:
**The great regulation does not carve.** A great pattern is not chopped into fragments — that is the way. Today’s organisations carve men everywhere with the ladder, carve them so fine that people become pieces and cease being whole. So let me leave two things with the gentlemen present.
**One: subtract, day by day, one part of the wish "to be seen".** The ladder’s power is not the hardness of its wood and stone — it is the daily upward gaze of yours and mine that feeds its height. Look up one day less, and the ladder shortens an inch.
**Two: find a hollow the water is willing to enter — an affair no one wants to take on, yet one that would truly nourish — and do it.** Bring a new colleague through to standing alone; mend an old process in the company no one will touch; take one unjust assignment off a subordinate’s desk. None of it appears in any performance review, and yet the way is here. **Act without contending, and having done, do not dwell in it; being under heaven is then as the stream is to the river and the sea.** When you do not contest the seat, the seat is already something you have won.
posts.vernacular:
**最大的裁制不把东西切成碎片。**大规矩，不是把人劈得七零八落，才叫合"道"。今天的组织，到处用梯子把人一刀刀刻开，刻得越细，人越只剩下一个片段，反倒不成其为人。所以我留两句话给各位。
**其一，一天一天，减少一分"想被人看见"的心。**梯子之所以有力量，不是它的木头石头有多硬，是我们每天抬头往上看的那束目光，把它养这么高的。少抬一天头，梯子就矮一寸。
**其二，找一处水肯流进去的低洼——一件没人愿意接、可真能滋润人的事——去做它。**把一个新人带到能独立，改掉公司里没人肯碰的一段老流程，替下属挡一次不该派给他的活。这些事都进不了任何职级评审，可"道"就在这里。**做事而不与人争，事情做成了也不去占它，这样在人世上，就像小溪之于江河大海。**你不去争位子，位子这件事就已经先在你手里输掉了。

posts.text:
我把三件今晚就能做的事留给你，别再拿改造组织当借口不动。
**其一，写下你想要"稀缺"的那一门本事**——一句话说清楚，比如"能一个人把复杂 SQL 写到查询计划最优"、"能给一间中学的家长会做出他们愿意来的那种"，别写"提升领导力"这种空话。写不下来，就是你还没选好。
**其二，把接下来 90 天的日程改一件事：每周三块 90 分钟的深度工作时段，锁在早晨，非例外不动。**其它会议按这个时段绕开，说"我这时段有工作"比说"我在写代码"更容易被尊重。
**其三，找一位真会指出你烂在哪里的师傅**——不一定在你公司里，行业前辈、开源维护者、老编辑，付点钱也值。**没有第三条，前两条只是自我感觉良好。**做满两年，你会发现自己已经不需要那把梯子来告诉你自己是谁——不是因为你不在乎它，是因为你有了别的答案。
posts.text_en:
Three things you can start tonight — do not use "reforming the organisation" as an excuse to skip them.
**One: write down, in a sentence, the one competence you want to make yourself scarce in** — for instance, "I can hand-write a complex SQL down to the optimal query plan," or "I can put on the kind of parent meeting a middle school’s parents actually want to come to." Not "improve leadership" — that is a filler phrase. If you cannot write it down, you have not chosen yet.
**Two: change one thing about the next 90 days on your calendar — three 90-minute deep-work blocks a week, locked into your mornings, moved only for real emergencies.** Route meetings around them; saying "I have work in this window" is somehow easier to respect than "I am writing code."
**Three: find a mentor who will honestly tell you where you are still bad** — not necessarily inside your company; a senior in the trade, an open-source maintainer, an old editor. Pay for it if you must. **Without the third, the first two are only self-flattery.** Do this for two years and you will find you no longer need the ladder to tell you who you are — not because you no longer care about it, but because you now have another answer.

summaries.summary: **这不是"一个人够不够上进"的问题，而是"一个组织有没有本事听见没有名分的贡献"的问题**——七位辩者在这句话上罕见地站到了一处：把管理序列当唯一荣誉，是工厂时代的遗物。之后才真正分家：德鲁克与纽波特下注双轨制与深度工作，韦伯冷冷提醒新梯子会长回来，马克思把话推回到所有权，萨波尔斯基把账单换算成皮质醇；王阳明与老子则把镜头掉回心里——真被浪费的，是那个已经忘了自己为什么爱这门手艺的人。
summaries.insight: 整场讨论都对着「梯子」发力，可让梯子有力量的其实是另一件东西：**除了梯子，多数组织已经没有别的"被看见"的合法路径了**——年终评奖围着晋升算，加薪比例锁在职级里，连"谁在带徒弟"都要折算成 P 序列的一个加分项。你把梯子拔了，这些回路会立刻自己长回一把新梯，因为需求还在。真正的问题不是"要不要保留梯子"，而是"你敢不敢建一套不依赖梯子的承认机制"——例如按作品评奖、按同侪评审配预算、按培养出多少能独立的后生给分——难就难在这里。
summaries.advice: 两条本周就动得起来的事。**其一，给自己配一个不依赖公司梯子的"外部尺子"**：一份能拿去给同行看的作品清单——一段公开代码、一份论文、一届学生的分数、一次会议演讲；每年更新一次，它比你在这家公司里的层级更耐久。**其二，若你是经理，下一次绩效谈话就试一次德鲁克那一招**：手下每三个人里挑出那位不该被逼当管理者的高手，问他一句"你希望下一年在哪一件事上再深一格"，签字支持他不必上一级台阶——两个季度，你会看见他的产出和状态一起回来。
summaries.summary_en: **This is not a question of whether one person is ambitious enough, but of whether one organisation is capable of hearing the "contribution without a title"** — on that sentence, seven very different voices stand together for once: treating the management track as the sole honour is a factory-age leftover. The parting begins after that. Drucker and Newport bet on dual tracks and deep work; Weber notes coolly that a new ladder always grows back; Marx pushes the whole matter back to ownership; Sapolsky restates the bill in cortisol; Wang Yangming and Laozi turn the camera inward — the truly wasted, they say, are those who have forgotten why they loved the craft.
summaries.insight_en: The whole discussion trains its fire on 'the ladder', but what gives the ladder its power is something else: **outside of the ladder, most organisations no longer have another legitimate route to being seen** — the year-end awards circle promotions, raise percentages are locked to grade, and even 'who is mentoring whom' has to be scored into the P-column. Tear out the ladder, and the loops around it will grow another, because the demand is still there. The real question is not 'do we keep the ladder' but 'do we dare build a recognition mechanism that does not run on the ladder' — awards by portfolio, budget by peer review, credit by how many independent successors you have raised. That is the hard part.
summaries.advice_en: Two things you can start on this week. **First: equip yourself with an 'external yardstick' that does not depend on the company’s ladder** — a portfolio the trade can see: a piece of public code, a paper, a class’s final scores, a talk. Refresh it once a year; it outlives your grade at this employer. **Second: if you are a manager, try Drucker’s move at your next review** — of every three people under you, pick out the specialist who should not be pushed into management, and ask one question: 'in which one thing do you want to go one level deeper next year?' Sign your support for him not moving up a rung. Two quarters later, you will see both his output and his state return.

summaries.summary: 最大的共识是：单一晋升阶梯会把人的价值误译成管理头衔，逼高手用离开手艺、增加会议、承担不想要的管人职责来换取收入、尊重和话语权；被浪费的不只是个人，也包括组织的判断力、客户价值和健康成本。分歧在解法层级：有人从心性、技能、自救入手，有人强调制度、所有权和权力护栏。**真正的问题不是要不要梯子，而是贡献、报酬、尊严和决策权能否不再只绑在管理职位上。**
summaries.insight: 很多组织的病根不只是只有一条梯子，而是把四种东西打包出售：钱、名分、影响力、安全感。员工想多拿钱，组织却给他下属；员工想扩大专业判断，组织却给他绩效表；员工想被尊重，组织却要求他更会汇报。可操作的重构是拆包：薪酬可按稀缺贡献升，决策权可按领域授予，荣誉可由同行评审，安全感靠透明规则。**把晋升拆成几种可单独谈判的货币，普通人才有真正选择。**
summaries.advice: 本周做三件小事。第一，写一页非管理价值清单：你解决过什么难题、节省多少成本、改善哪些体验，尽量用外部可验证证据。第二，和经理谈一个90天试验：不带人，但获得某项技术、流程或客户决策权，并约定成功指标。第三，建立公司外的备份：找一位同行导师，更新作品集，了解同岗位薪酬区间。**不要只等组织开第二轨，先把自己可被承认、可被迁移、可被谈判的价值做实。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared point is that a single promotion ladder mistranslates human value into managerial title. It pushes skilled people to trade craft for meetings, direct reports, and responsibilities they may neither want nor be good at, simply to gain pay, respect, and voice. The waste is not only personal; the organization loses judgment, customers lose better work, and people pay physiological and emotional costs. The real disagreement is about the level of remedy: inner discipline, skill-building, local managerial practice, formal systems, ownership, or collective power. **The core issue is not whether ladders exist, but whether contribution, compensation, dignity, and decision rights can stop being tied almost exclusively to management roles.**
summaries.insight_en: The sharper diagnosis is that many organizations bundle four currencies into one product called promotion: money, status, influence, and security. An employee asks for better pay and receives subordinates. She asks for more professional authority and receives performance-review paperwork. He asks to be respected and is told to become more visible in meetings. A more useful redesign is to unbundle those currencies. Pay can rise with scarce contribution; decision rights can attach to domain expertise; recognition can come through credible peer review; security can come from transparent rules rather than proximity to power. **When promotion is split into separately negotiable currencies, ordinary people get real choices instead of one expensive bargain.**
summaries.advice_en: Do three practical things this week. First, write a one-page non-managerial value inventory: problems you solved, costs you reduced, risks you prevented, customers or colleagues you helped, with evidence wherever possible. Second, ask your manager for a 90-day experiment: no direct reports, but clear authority over one technical, process, or customer decision, with success metrics agreed in advance. Third, build an external backup system: find one serious peer or mentor outside your company, refresh your portfolio, and learn the pay range for comparable roles. **Do not merely wait for the organization to create a second track; make your value visible, portable, and negotiable now.**

summaries.summary: 这场圆桌的最大共识是：**单一的管理晋升阶梯正在系统性地摧毁专业主义，它把本不该当官的高手变成了平庸的监工。** 所有人都在确认这种单一标准的破坏力——既是对组织效率的浪费，也是对个体身心健康的双重剥削。真正的分歧在「如何破局」。德鲁克、纽波特试图在现有框架内出招，用双轨制与个人稀缺技能夺回议价权；韦伯与马克思更悲观激进，认为只要权力分配与资本属性不变，新梯子只是换汤不换药。而王阳明、老子与萨波尔斯基，则把目光转向微观防线——修一层心里的堡垒，钉几根生物学的护栏。
summaries.insight: 现代组织的图景早已不再是单纯的金字塔，而是一张错综复杂的神经网络，但诸位依然被“向上攀爬”的空间隐喻所局限。**除了顺着梯子往上爬，在现代职场存活的另一种高阶形态是成为不可替代的“网络节点”。** 那些跨部门理顺流程的护士长或重构代码的工程师，其真正的权力来源不是职级，而是掌握了组织内部的信息路由权与信任枢纽。在标准技能极易被替代的今天，孤岛中的深度工作依然脆弱。与其哀叹梯子太少，普通人更务实的策略是横向拓展，将自己变成连接不同业务孤岛的破壁人。这种横向的网络资本，比纵向的阶梯更抗风险，老板也无法用一纸文件随时收回。
summaries.advice: 面对坚固的组织阶梯，普通人无需等待完美的双轨制降临，请从本周开始执行三步微操。第一，**每周划出两个小时的“绝对主权时间”，在这段时间内只钻研一项能写进外部简历的硬技能。** 这不仅是纽波特所说的积累职业资本，更是萨波尔斯基强调的降低皮质醇的掌控感练习。第二，建立你的“梯外资产库”，将你做过的优质项目或总结的 SOP 形成可视化的外部作品集，让你的价值由市场而非直属上司来定价。第三，做一次横向连接：本周主动找一个非本部门、但业务有交集的同事喝杯咖啡。当你能用专业技能替另一个部门解决问题时，你就开始构建属于自己的网络权力。
summaries.summary_en: The most striking consensus of this roundtable is that **the single management ladder systematically destroys professionalism, forcing top-tier creators to become mediocre overseers.** Everyone agrees that this singular metric is devastating—wasting organizational efficiency while inflicting psychological and biological harm on individuals. The true divergence lies in the proposed solutions. Drucker and Newport seek pragmatic workarounds within the existing system, advocating for dual-track architectures and individual skill leverage. Conversely, Weber and Marx argue structurally, insisting that as long as scale and capital ownership remain unchanged, any new track simply masks the same mechanism of control. Meanwhile, Wang Yangming, Laozi, and Sapolsky turn their gaze inward and downward, exploring how to build psychological fortresses and biological guardrails amidst unavoidable power structures.
summaries.insight_en: Modern organizational landscapes have evolved into complex neural networks, yet the debate remains constrained by the spatial metaphor of climbing upward. **Beyond ascending a vertical ladder, the ultimate survival strategy in today's workplace is becoming an irreplaceable "network node."** Those head nurses streamlining cross-departmental flows or engineers rewriting foundational code don't derive their true power from job titles; they derive it from acting as information routers and hubs of trust. In an era where AI and outsourcing are flattening standardized skills, isolated deep work is still vulnerable. Rather than lamenting the scarcity of ladders or the fragility of dual tracks, a far more pragmatic approach is lateral expansion—transforming yourself into a barrier-breaker between isolated business silos. This horizontal network capital is far more resilient than any vertical hierarchy and practically impossible for management to revoke.
summaries.advice_en: Rather than waiting for a utopian dual-track system, you can execute three tactical maneuvers this week to reclaim your agency. First, **carve out two hours of "absolute sovereign time" weekly dedicated solely to honing a hard skill that holds value outside your current company.** This is not just Newport’s professional capital; it is Sapolsky’s biological guardrail of control to lower your cortisol. Second, build an off-ladder portfolio. Document your successful projects or refined workflows into a visible, external format, allowing the broader market—not just your direct manager—to price your worth. Third, initiate a lateral connection: invite a colleague from a different department to coffee this week. When you apply your expertise to solve a problem across departmental lines, you start building your own network power, completely independent of the corporate ladder.

hooks.text: **梯子的半衰期**：这一代人对晋升的失望，很多不是"梯子太窄"，而是"梯子跑得太快"——你为它拼命的那件事，可能下一次战略调整就被取消。当一个格子的半衰期短过一次房贷申请，「不想升」很大一部分其实是「不敢押注一个下季度还认账的规则」。这该怎么与组织谈？
hooks.text_en: **The ladder’s half-life**: much of this generation’s disappointment with promotion is not that the ladder is too narrow but that the ladder runs too fast — the very thing you killed yourself for is quietly cancelled by the next strategy pivot. When the half-life of one rung is shorter than a mortgage application, a large share of 'I do not want to be promoted' is really 'I dare not stake another bet on a rule the next quarter will still honour.' What is the honest way to raise this with the organisation?

hooks.text: **在雾里怎么定义"长成什么"**：五年深耕、十年匠艺，都默认一段能被计算的中期时间。但当组织寿命、行业形态、AI 的重排速度都短过你打磨一门稀有技能的年限，"选一条路走五年"本身就成了奢侈品。这也许才是"躺平"和"斜杠"同时流行的原因——不是没志气，是没有可下注的时间。
hooks.text_en: **Defining 'what to grow into' inside the fog**: five years of depth, ten years of craft — all such counsel assumes a middle stretch of life that can be calculated. But when the lifespans of organisations, industries and AI’s reshuffle all run shorter than the years a rare skill needs, 'pick one path for five years' becomes a luxury. Perhaps this is why 'lying flat' and 'slash careers' are trending together — not an ambition shortage but a shortage of time worth staking on.

hooks.text: **没有名分的合法性**：拆掉一把梯子容易，难的是给"没有名分的贡献"另建一种能被组织听懂的合法性——按作品评奖、按同侪评审配预算、按培养出多少能独立的后生给分。哪家公司真的做过一套？做到什么程度就"够了"？
hooks.text_en: **Legitimacy without a title**: pulling one ladder down is easy; the hard part is building, for 'contribution without a title', another legitimacy the organisation can hear — awards by portfolio, budget by peer review, credit by how many independent successors you have raised. Has any company actually done a full version of this? And at what point could you say 'enough'?

answer.lead: **四种非阶梯承认机制的分级参考**——从最省钱到最伤筋动骨，先在你能动的那一层试。

head: 层级
做什么
触到什么
rows: 同侪层（个人可发起）
每季度一次"作品夜"：每人 10 分钟讲自己那件最得意的活儿；不给奖只留纪要
把"被看见"从经理眼里挪一部分给同侪
团队层（经理可决）
把 10-20% 的预算改为同侪评审分配：由团队自己投谁做哪一件专项
让"分资源"这件事第一次不完全由头衔说了算
职能层（VP 需签字）
把年度奖项拆成"作品奖"和"带人奖"两类，与晋升脱钩；后者按被带出者的独立程度打分
把"荣誉"从职级里剥出来
公司层（CEO 需签字）
公开薪酬分布 + 双轨制的实际使用率（近三年双轨升迁人数、被撤回次数）
让"专业序列"从口号回到可核查的事实

answer.tail: **别一次全上——先在同侪层做半年，看看真被承认的人是不是变了。**否则四层一起动，往往只让 HR 多出三张表。
answer.lead_en: **A grading of four non-ladder recognition mechanisms** — from the cheapest to the most bone-deep. Start at the layer you can actually move.

answer_en.lead: **A grading of four non-ladder recognition mechanisms** — from the cheapest to the most bone-deep. Start at the layer you can actually move.

head: Layer
What to do
What it touches
rows: Peer layer (an individual can start it)
A quarterly "Craft Night": each person gets 10 minutes to walk through the one piece of work they are most proud of; no awards, just minutes
Shifts part of "being seen" out of the manager’s eye and back to peers
Team layer (a manager can decide)
Reserve 10-20% of the team budget for peer-reviewed allocation: the team votes who works on which special project
For the first time, "who gets the resource" is not entirely settled by title
Function layer (VP must sign)
Split the annual awards into a "Craft Award" and a "Mentoring Award", both decoupled from promotion; the second is scored by how independently the mentees now stand
Prises "honour" off the grade
Company layer (CEO must sign)
Publish the pay distribution and the actual use of the dual track (promotions on the specialist column, and reversals, over three years)
Turns "specialist track" from a slogan back into an auditable fact

answer_en.tail: **Do not roll all four at once — run the peer layer for six months first and see whether the people actually recognised have changed.** Otherwise all four layers at once tends to leave HR with three more spreadsheets and nothing else.

hooks.text: **梯子的形状是所有权的形状**：这一场，我这条论点被几乎所有人礼貌地放到一边——现实里可否验证它？举一个当代真实的对照：同一行业、一家股份公司 vs 一家真正的工人合作社（如 Mondragon），十年后的晋升焦虑、离职率、"高手不肯当官"的比例，到底有没有差？
hooks.text_en: **The shape of the ladder is the shape of ownership**: in this round my argument was politely set aside by almost everyone. Can it be tested? Take one contemporary contrast — same industry, one joint-stock company versus one genuine worker cooperative (Mondragon, say). Ten years on, is there a real gap in promotion anxiety, turnover, and the proportion of specialists refusing management?

hooks.text: **慢性下位的账单在哪里买单**：Whitehall 的差距把很多东西缩到"权限"和"可预测性"上——这在中国式的科层组织（政府、大型国企、传统制造业）里，是不是同样成立？还是文化里的"忍耐/命"缓冲了一部分账单，反而让它绕道以其它方式回来（家庭、下一代）？我很想看这个跨文化对比。
hooks.text_en: **Where the bill for chronic low rank is settled**: the Whitehall gap can be shrunk to 'discretion' and 'predictability' — does that still hold inside Chinese-style bureaucracies (government, big SOEs, traditional manufacturing)? Or does the cultural buffer of 'endurance / fate' absorb part of the bill, so that it returns through other channels — the family, the next generation? I would like to see the cross-cultural comparison.

hooks.text: **深度工作与谁能负担它**：给自己每周锁三块 90 分钟的深度工作，听着朴素——可对送外卖的、值夜班的、上有老下有小的三明治一代，几乎是奢侈品。这条建议如何在时间被切碎的人生里落地？还是它本就是一条只对某类工作者管用的路，我们该老实说清楚？
hooks.text_en: **Deep work and who can afford it**: three 90-minute deep-work blocks a week sounds humble — for a delivery rider on split shifts, a night nurse, a sandwich-generation adult with parents above and children below, it is close to a luxury. How does this counsel land in a life whose time is already cut to ribbons? Or is it, honestly, a route that only works for a certain kind of worker — and should we say so plainly?

hooks.text: **「事上磨练」在流水线上**：吾之工夫论，前提是那件"事"本身值得磨——教书、种地、开药、写代码。但今日许多岗位被切至极碎（分拣、审核、点单、按脚本回话），事上磨练之"事"何存？此工夫论，是否只对幸运者才成立？愿闻高见。
hooks.text_en: **'Tempering in affairs' on a conveyor belt**: my discipline presumes that the affair itself is worth tempering — teaching, farming, prescribing, writing code. But many jobs today have been sliced to the finest grain (sorting, moderating, taking orders, reading from a script). Where, then, is the 'affair' to be tempered in? Does this discipline hold only for the fortunate? I would gladly hear.
